title: Decision: a did_webvh leaf's MIMI user URI is the one mimi: URI in its head DID document's alsoKnownAs; contacts pin user URI -> SCID
description:
Question: in a MIMI room, which user URI (mimi://<domain>/u/<id>) does a did_webvh leaf belong to?

Sources. draft-atwood-mls-didwebvh-credential-01 §Binding to the LeafNode: "The SCID of the log is the credential's identity." §Reference Identifiers: the presented identifier is the SCID; applications SHOULD pin the SCID "for each contact the first time it is learned", SHOULD compare it on every later credential for that contact, MUST alert the user if a contact's SCID changes, and SHOULD display the DID string. The draft does not say how a credential is tied to a contact, i.e. to a MIMI user URI. protocol-07 names users by URI in the participant list, room policy, KeyMaterial and franking (§5.4.1.3: "the sender's identity in its credential ... matches the sender_uri"), and the hub authorizes by those URIs (§9). Today a BasicCredential's identity is the user URI (decision mimid-1wgh.6.1). mimi-protocol#159 leaves the credential-to-domain rule open; mimid's rule is that the identity's domain is the provider's (decisions mimid-1wgh.6.9, mimid-1wgh.7.10).

Readings:
(a) The user URI is listed by the controller in the head DID document's alsoKnownAs (DID Core: other identifiers of the same subject). A did_webvh leaf's member identity is the one alsoKnownAs entry with the mimi: scheme; none or several = no member identity, so the leaf cannot be authorized (fails closed). The user's update keys sign it, so the provider cannot rebind an SCID to another user, and the hub keeps authorizing by user URI with the existing domain check (URI domain = submitting provider). Contacts pin user URI -> SCID.
(b) Derive the URI from the DID string: did:webvh:<scid>:<domain>:u:<id> <-> mimi://<domain>/u/<id>. No extra field, but invents a syntactic mapping, forces the DID to be hosted by the MIMI provider, and the DID string changes when a DID moves.
(c) Use the DID (or SCID) itself as the participant's URI in the participant list and policy. Breaks every place that takes a domain from a user URI (routing, KeyMaterial, the credential-to-domain rule, franking's senderUri) and needs protocol changes.
(d) Carry the user URI in a LeafNode extension or app component signed only by the device key. New wire format; a device (or a provider that holds no update key but can mint a new DID) could claim any URI without the controller's signature.

Chosen: (a), INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC. Least invention: no new wire field (alsoKnownAs exists in DID Core and did:webvh documents), the hub and agents keep using user URIs everywhere, and the controller's signature covers the binding. mimi-mls reports a did_webvh leaf's member identity (Observer::members, CommitDetail, Incoming sender, welcome_sender) as that URI, and its SCID separately. The hub applies its existing rules to that URI. The agent pins user URI -> SCID in state.json on first sight (KeyMaterial/fetch, a Welcome's tree, an incoming Commit); a later leaf for the same user with another SCID is refused when the agent adds it, and reported as Event::IdentityChanged otherwise (the draft's MUST alert). A BasicCredential leaf for a user pinned to an SCID counts as a change too (refused when adding, alerted otherwise): otherwise the user's provider could add a BasicCredential device for a did_webvh user, the very thing the draft exists to stop. The draft's pin text does not say this; feedback item 22.
The controller side (mls_didwebvh::controller::DidLog) gains a way to write alsoKnownAs, kept by later entries.
For -01: say how an application ties a credential to its own user name (alsoKnownAs or otherwise), since MIMI and most messengers name users by something other than the SCID. Feedback item 22.
notes:
Implemented in 16bb4ee (controller alsoKnownAs), 114b25c (mimi-mls member identity), 088d81f (hub, KeyPackage upload), a2ded35 (agent pins). Left open for Mark (label human). Feedback item 22.
